finding: The existing packet/cortex authority is deliberately text/information-packet-only. VoiceOutputPacket carries packet identity, text, planned duration, playback_state, heard_fraction, interruption_ms, commit_eligible and VoiceOutcome binding, but no PCM/audio artifact reference. The existing Kokoro/Piper benchmark is a separate already-routed TTS runtime boundary that yields real incremental float-audio chunks and exact WAV hashes. Therefore the first composed owner-VPS FDX run must bind these two existing authorities in its execution receipt/harness rather than adding a second playback state machine or widening VoiceOutputPacket solely for the test.
required_execution_binding: For each generated TTS output, create exactly one run-local delivery binding keyed by the existing VoiceOutputPacket.packet_id and the exact voice_session_id/turn_id/causal lineage already owned by the cortex/session authorities.

For every producer chunk actually admitted to the headless sink, record monotonic sequence, sample_rate, sample_count, byte_count or canonical float/PCM byte representation, SHA-256 and first/last delivery timestamps. The receipt must make it impossible to claim delivery for chunks that were only generated but never admitted to the sink.

Do not create a second canonical playback state machine. Existing VoiceOutputPacket playback_state/heard_fraction/interruption_ms/commit_eligible remains the semantic state authority; the run-local audio binding is evidence that physical-independent bytes crossed the exact sink boundary corresponding to that packet.

On FDX3/FDX4 barge-in, stop consuming the producer iterator or close/cancel it when supported, immediately stop admitting further chunks to the sink binding, and mark all post-cancel generated/discarded chunks separately. Generated-after-cancel bytes MUST NOT be counted as delivered/heard/commit-eligible.

If the producer cannot be interrupted internally, classify producer_cancel_capability=false but still test the existing delivery-boundary cancellation. Do not convert sink cancellation into mid-generation producer-cancel credit.
For a partially delivered interrupted output, assert commit_eligible=false and VoiceOutcome durable-result exclusion even though one or more real audio chunks crossed the headless sink boundary.

For the replacement output, require a complete admitted chunk sequence, exact aggregate audio SHA-256/sample count, VoiceOutputPacket terminal completed state, heard-result/VoiceOutcome binding and subsequent canonical persistence/reentry identity.
Persist the delivery binding only as execution evidence/receipt unless an existing admitted canonical schema already provides the exact field. Do not invent a new durable Voice truth store.

acceptance_discriminator.FDX3: At least one real local TTS chunk is sink-admitted for the old output, user barge-in is admitted, no later chunk is sink-admitted for that packet after cancel boundary, old packet stays non-commit-eligible, and replacement output completes.
acceptance_discriminator.FDX4: Concurrent user-over-output produces the same fail-closed delivery and stale-result behavior with exact monotonic ordering; late/stale tool or old output result cannot become durable state.
acceptance_discriminator.FDX6: Only the fully heard replacement result is written through the existing canonical persistence integration; close/reopen and existing restart/reentry/fresh-turn authorities preserve the exact causal lineage without duplicate durable output.

explicit_zero_credit: true TTS producer cancellation when only sink cancellation executes
whole voice e2e until exact composed owner-VPS run passes
